sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 276 PDF pages
sources.locator: section 5.1.1 printed p. 210 (PDF p. 217): the warning that Newtonian-limit coefficients must be compared in one and the same coordinate system; section 6.1 printed pp. 232-233 (PDF pp. 239-240): the Schwarzschild metric (6.1), the horizon r = 2GM and the coordinate breakdown; section 6.1.1 printed pp. 233-235 (PDF pp. 240-242): Birkhoff's theorem and the reduced form; section 6.1.2 printed pp. 236-237 (PDF pp. 243-244): the Kretschmann invariant and its finiteness at r = 2GM; section 6.1.3 printed pp. 238-240 (PDF pp. 245-247): the tortoise coordinate and the ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein form; section 6.1.4 printed pp. 245-249 (PDF pp. 252-256): Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates and the singularity at r = 0; section 6.2 printed pp. 249-251 (PDF pp. 256-258): the gravitational redshift; section 6.3 printed pp. 252-258 (PDF pp. 259-265): circular orbits, the ISCO and the photon sphere.

contents.name: section 6.1 (6.1): the Schwarzschild metric and its domain r > 2GM
contents.support: The datum of clause (b)-(d) has exactly the metric components displayed in (6.1) with s = 2G_N m_*/c^2, and the domain r > s is the source's domain r > 2GM in geometrized units.

contents.name: section 6.1.1: Birkhoff's theorem, metric independent of t
contents.support: The theorem is not quoted; the page proves the local warped-product version with explicit hypotheses (z != 0, connected base) and records that no global uniqueness is asserted.

contents.name: section 6.1.2 (6.3): R_{mu nu rho sigma}R^{mu nu rho sigma} = 48G^2M^2/r^6
contents.support: Clause (c) proves K = 12s^2/r^6 = 48G_N^2m_*^2/(c^4r^6) directly from the orthonormal-frame components; the source's value is the same in geometrized units.

contents.name: section 6.1.2: the horizon is not a curvature singularity
contents.support: The remark separates the chart breakdown at r = s from the curvature obstruction at r = 0 using the page's own extension and Kruskal items rather than the source's diagram-level argument.

contents.name: section 6.1.3 (6.6)-(6.8): tortoise coordinate and ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein form
contents.support: The extension lemma constructs exactly this advanced-chart metric with a time orientation field, proves smoothness and nondegeneracy at r = s, and records the determinant -r^4 sin^2(theta).

contents.name: section 6.1.4 (6.12)-(6.15): Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates and implicit radial relation
contents.support: The Kruskal datum is the same construction with s = 2GM; the implicit relation UV = -(r/s-1)e^{r/s} is the source's relation in rescaled coordinates, with existence and smoothness of r proved in the companion lemma.

contents.name: section 6.1.4: the four regions and their interpretation
contents.support: Clause (c) proves the four-component decomposition and the explicit isometries with the exterior and interior branches, including the second exterior region.

contents.name: section 6.2: gravitational redshift between static observers
contents.support: The theorem derives the observer-energy ratio from the conserved Killing pairing along a future null geodesic, with the source's ratio as the special case of static emitters and receivers; no measurement is reported.

contents.name: section 6.3: conserved quantities and the effective potential for geodesics
contents.support: The lemma proves the constancy of e and ell, the equatorial reduction and the radial equation with the effective potential W_ell, matching the source's reduction.

contents.name: section 6.3: circular orbits, ISCO at r = 6GM and the photon sphere at r = 3GM
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(d) prove existence for r_0 > 3s/2, the necessity of the threshold, the stability sign at r = 3s and the null orbit at r = 3s/2, the source's values in units s = 2GM.

contents.name: section 6.4 and later: collapse, formation and observational discussion
contents.reason: Collapse/formation theorems and observational comparisons need matter evolution and primary reports (an experimental-interface page); the spherical vacuum page asserts no singularity theorem, no collapse and no observation, so these sections are deliberately not built here.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 5 printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149): Killing vectors and conserved quantities; Ch. 7 printed pp. 164-192 (PDF pp. 171-199): the general spherically symmetric metric (7.4)-(7.13), the Schwarzschild metric (7.29), the curvature invariant (7.30), the effective potential and orbits, the tortoise coordinate, the Eddington-Finkelstein and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates (7.74)-(7.85) and the singularity at r = 0.

contents.name: Ch. 7 (7.4)-(7.13): the general spherically symmetric metric with sphere factor r^2 dOmega^2
contents.support: The product-chart construction of clause (b) with the areal radius r and the round sphere factor is the coordinate form the source derives; the page states the domain r > s rather than assuming one.

contents.name: Ch. 7 (7.29): ds^2 = -(1-2GM/r)dt^2 + (1-2GM/r)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2
contents.support: The Christoffel symbols of clauses (a)-(d) are computed for exactly this metric with f = 1 - s/r; the source's geometrized form is the case s = 2GM.

contents.name: Ch. 7 (7.30): the curvature invariant of the Schwarzschild metric
contents.support: The directly computed value 12s^2/r^6 is used; the source's printed numerical coefficient differs from the direct computation by a factor 4 and is not inherited (recorded in the item's remark and in these notes).

contents.name: Ch. 7: static observers, redshift and the weak-field limit of the clock ratio
contents.support: Clause (c) proves the proper-time identity and the clock-ratio formula for the congruence n = f^{-1/2} partial_0; the source's later redshift discussion is used only through the exact ratio.

contents.name: Ch. 7: the geodesic equation, effective potential and stability of circular orbits
contents.support: The threshold r_0 > 3s/2, the ISCO at r = 3s and the photon sphere at r = 3s/2 are proved from the reduced radial equation with the second-derivative sign computed explicitly.

contents.name: Ch. 7: the breakdown of Schwarzschild coordinates at r = 2GM
contents.support: The lemma proves the breakdown is a chart-coefficient divergence by constructing the advanced chart and verifying regularity at r = s.

contents.name: Ch. 7 (7.74)-(7.85): Kruskal diagram, null horizon and the singularity at r = 0
contents.support: The smooth metric, the null axes and the curvature growth towards UV = 1 are proved; the singularity statement is restricted to the exact curvature-continuity obstruction of the page's remark.

sources.title: P. K. Townsend, Black Holes, arXiv:gr-qc/9707012v1 (1997), 35 pages
sources.locator: section 2.3 printed pp. 15-25: the Schwarzschild metric (2.32); section 2.3.1 printed p. 19: the one-way membrane at r = 2M; section 2.3.2 printed p. 21: the Kruskal-Szekeres form (2.56)-(2.57); section 2.3.3 printed p. 25: the isotropic form (2.60) and conformal flatness of the t = const slices.

contents.name: section 2.3 (2.32): the Schwarzschild metric in units G = c = 1
contents.support: Clauses (b)-(c) prove the vanishing of Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors for f = 1 - s/r; the source states the same solution in geometrized units.

contents.name: section 2.3.1: the horizon as a one-way membrane
contents.support: The lemma replaces the informal membrane picture by the exact cone criterion, monotonicity of U and V, and the escape definition with its proved non-escaping set {U >= 0}.

contents.name: section 2.3.2 (2.56)-(2.57): the Kruskal-Szekeres form extended by analytic continuation
contents.support: The metric components -2s^3 e^{-r/s}/r dU dV + r^2 dOmega^2 and the implicit relation are the source's expressions with s = 2M.

contents.name: section 2.3.3 (2.60): the isotropic form and the statement that t = const slices are conformally flat
contents.support: Clause (a)-(c) prove the exact conversion r = rho(1+s/(4rho))^2, the conformally flat spatial form and the leading areal-radius shift; the source's form is the resulting expression.

contents.name: section 2.5 and later: charged and rotating black holes
contents.reason: The design reserves charged and rotating solutions for later modules; the spherical vacuum page deliberately contains no axisymmetric or charged model, so these sections can only be built after their own A/B pair is scaffolded.

contents.name: section 4: black-hole thermodynamics and asymptotic charges
contents.reason: Temperature, entropy and ADM-type charges require asymptotic definitions and surface-flux mathematics that the local-and-global-energy page explicitly defers; no such claim is made on the spherical vacuum page.
